approved: Asbestos Safety and Eradication Agency Bill 2013

Supported the Asbestos Safety and Eradication Agency Bill 2013, citing continuing asbestos risks, fragmented regulation and the need for all levels of government to participate, while questioning funding of $10½ million compared with $12.3 million.

Supported the Asbestos Safety and Eradication Agency Bill 2013, urged education warnings for home renovators, reported community and personal impacts of asbestos disease, and called for research, prevention and cross-party action.

Introduced the Asbestos Safety and Eradication Agency Bill 2013 to implement the Asbestos Management Review's recommendations, citing International Labour Organization figures that someone worldwide dies of an asbestos-related disease every five minutes, and said the first national strategic plan for asbestos eradication is due by 1 July this year.

The Asbestos Safety and Eradication Agency Bill 2013 was supported, establishing a national agency to coordinate asbestos safety and eradication, with Australia facing an estimated 13,000 mesothelioma cases by 2020 and 40,000 other asbestos-related cancers. The coalition criticised a $1.8 million funding cut from the originally pledged $12.3 million to $10.5 million, and urged broader state representation on the agency's council and expanded research functions.
